title: Particle Lenia (new class): from a random particle soup, dense boxes self-assemble into closed particle rings with a few particles inside, coexisting with a particle gas; at lower density, bilayer-like ribbons
summary: Particle Lenia (Mordvintsev et al. 2022: overdamped particles descend E = R - G(U), with U a ring-kernel sum over neighbours) in a periodic 60x60 box with the benchmark parameters, started from uniformly random positions. At 3500 particles (scan1.png, seed 0, and pack, seed 1) a few hundred closed rings of ~15-25 particles, many holding 1-4 particles inside, form by t~25-50 and persist to t=600 (labkit: 37 persistent tracks, density rim/core 1.48, rim/outside 5.8) in coexistence with a dense particle gas; some rings elongate into two-lobed peanuts. At 2500 particles the soup becomes long double-stranded ribbons (bilayer-like) that fold into labyrinths, at 1500 a foam of open networks.
